s: On adding common salt to water, the boiling point and freezing point of water will :
x: Salt dissolved in water raises its boiling point (boiling point elevation), and it also lowers the freezing point (depression). So the boiling point increases and the freezing point decreases respectively.

s: Sound wave in air is –
x: Sound waves in air (and in any fluid medium) are longitudinal waves because particles of the medium through which sound is transported, vibrate parallel to the direction that the sound wave moves. 4. What do we call the distance between two consecutive compressions of a sound wave? (a) Wave number (b) Frequency (c) Wavelength (d) Amplitude Jharkhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2023 Ans. (c) The distance between two consecutive compressions or two consequitive rarefactions is the wavelength of the sound wave which is a longitudinal wave in air or in any fluid medium. The speed of sound is the product of the wavelength and frequency of the wave. Wavelength in a transverse wave is the distance between two consecutive crests or troughs.

s: The alkaloid caffeine is present in :
x: Caffeine is a naturally occurring compound found in the leaves and fruits of certain plants. It is found in coffee, tea, cocoa, cola, soft drinks. As a stimulant, caffeine acts on the brain and nervous system. In small doses, it can make anyone feel refreshed and focused. While in large doses, it can make to feel anxious and have difficulty in sleeping.

s: Rocket works on the principle of the following :
x: An electric rocket engine is a jet engine in which material ejected backward (ionized gas in general) causes a forward thrust to the rocket (on the principle of conservation of momentum). The linear momentum (p) or simply momentum of a particle is the product of its mass and its velocity [ i.e. p = mv].

s: A dentist mirror is a –
x: Concave mirrors are used by dentists because at a short range (object distances less than the focal length) they produce magnified, upright images. It is useful to have a magnified image of a tooth when you’re looking for or repairing cavities, cracks or other abnormalities.

s: The power of a lens is measured in :
x: Dioptre is the unit of measurement for the refractive power of a lens. The power of a lens is defined as the reciprocal of its focal length in metres. D f = 1 where D is power of lens in dioptre and f is the focal length in metres. Converging lens has positive optical power and diverging lens has negative optical power.

s: Which one of the following types of the mirror is used to see the traffic behind the car?
x: Rear-view mirrors in vehicles are convex mirrors because they give a wider field of view and an erect, diminished image of the traffic behind. A concave mirror would give a narrow field of view and is used for headlights.

s: In Stethoscope, the sound of the patient's heartbeat reaches the doctor's ears by :
x: Stethoscopes work by the principle of multiple reflection of sound. When a doctor or nurse places a stethoscope diaphragm on a patient's chest, sound waves traveling through the patient's body cause the flat surface of the diaphragm to vibrate and because the vibrating object is attached to a tube, the sound waves are channeled in a specific direction. Each wave bounces, or reflects, off the inside walls of the rubber tube, a process called multiple reflection. In this way, each wave, in succession, reaches the eartips, or rubber nubs on the ends of the device, and finally the listener's eardrums.

s:
Which of the following statements is/are true in relation to sound waves?
Statement I : Speed of sound decreases when we go from solid to gaseous state Statement II : In any medium as we decrease the temperature, the speed of sound increases Statement III : Speed of sound is less in aluminium medium than in glass medium
o: Statement I, II and III all are true
Only Statement I and II are true
Only Statement II and III are true
x: The Speed of sound depends upon the nature of medium through which it propagates. Speed of sound is maximum in solids while minimum in gases. Speed of sound is less in glass medium than in aluminium medium. Increase in temperature results to increase in the speed of sound in any medium. Hence, among the given statement, only statement I is true.

s: Microwaves are electromagnetic waves having frequencies in range of :
x: Microwave is a form of electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths ranging from about one meter to one millimeter corresponding to frequencies between 300 MHz and 300 GHz respectively. Different sources define different frequency ranges as microwave; the above broad definition includes both UHF and EHF (millimeter wave) bands. Hence, option (c) is the most appropriate answer.

s: On which principle, a Jet Engine works?
x: Nearly all modern airplanes use jet propulsion to fly. Jet engines and rockets work on the principle of conservation of linear momentum.

s: Large number of thin strips of black paint are made on the surface of a convex lens of focal length 20 cm to catch the image of a white horse. The image will be:
o: More than one of the above
x: When light passes through a convex lens, it converges or comes together at a focal point. In this case, the convex lens has a focal length of 20 cm. When the lens has a large number of thin black strips on its surface, these strips will block or absorb some of the incident light. As a result, less light will reach the focal point and form the image. Hence, thin black strips on the surface of a convex lens will only reduce the intensity of the light but will not cast any shadow on the image, as it is quite thin. Thus, option (a) is the correct answer.

s: Myopia and Hypermetropia can be respectively corrected by :
x: Myopia (near-sightedness) and Hypermetropia (farsightedness) can be respectively corrected by concave and convex lens.

s: In driving a car which type of mirror would you like to use for observing traffic at your back ?
x: A convex mirror gives a much wider field of view of the traffic at your back than a plain mirror of the same size. It always forms an erect and diminished image and they also have a wider field of view as they are curved outwards.

s: What will be the nature of image formed by a convex mirror when the position of object is between infinity and pole P of the mirror?
x: When the position of object is between infinity and pole (P) of the convex mirror, then the image will be formed between the pole (P) and the focus (F) behind the mirror. The image thus formed is diminished, virtual and erect.

s: The density of milk is measured by?
x: A lactometer is the instrument used to check milk purity by measuring its specific gravity (density); a hydrometer is general-purpose, barometer measures pressure and hygrometer humidity.

s: An air bubble inside water behaves as a:
x: An air bubble in water is a region of lower refractive index than the surrounding water, so it is thinner at the edges relative to the medium and diverges light, acting as a divergent (concave) lens.

s: For the myopic eye, the defect is cured by :
x: In myopia the image forms in front of the retina, so a concave lens of negative power is used to diverge rays and correct it; a convex lens would worsen it.

s: An ice cube is floating in a glass of water. What happens to the water level when the ice melts? It –
x: According to Archimedes' principle, floating object displaces an amount of water equal to its own weight. Thus, the water level remains the same when the ice cube melts.

s: A distance of 1 km. means –
x: The SI unit for distance is metre. 1 Km. is equal to 1000m. 1 m is equal to 100 cm.

s: In a pressure cooker food is cooked in shorter time because –
o: The boiling point of water increases
The boiling point of water decreases
x: A pressure cooker raises the pressure, which raises the boiling point of water (~120 °C), so food cooks faster at the higher temperature.

s: Dispersion of light is possible by :
x: Dispersion of light is possible by prism. Upon passage through the prism, the white light is separated into its different component colours, which is known as dispersion.

s: Which one of the following changes occurs when salt is added into the water?
o: Boiling point is increased and freezing point decreased
Boiling point is decreased and freezing point is
Both boiling point and freezing point are decreased
Both boiling point and freezing point are increased
x: If salt is added to water then the boiling point of water will increase. This happens as the boiling point is the temperature at which the vapor pressure of solvent becomes equal to the external atmospheric pressure. Similarly it also decreases the freezing point, which in turn will interfere with the frozen solution's crystal structure. That means the temperature will have to be colder to overcome it and freeze the mixture.

s: To remove the defect of long sightedness one uses :
x: Far-sightedness (hypermetropia) as it is medically termed is a vision condition in which distant object are usually seen clear, but near objects are not clearly visible. To remove this vision problem one should use a convex lens.

s: An air bubble in water will act like a :
x: An air bubble in water, whose surface is convex will act like a concave lens (divergent lens). The refractive index of water is more than that of air. Thus the nature of lens of submerged water bubble is changed.

s: Which one of the following statement is not true for a person suffering from hypermetropia?
o: The person can see far objects distinctly
The focal length of the lens is large
The image of the close objects is focused behind the
A concave lens is used to correct this defect
x: Far-sightedness (hypermetropia) is a common vision problem, affecting about a fourth of the population. People with hypermetropia can see distant objects very well but have difficulty in focusing on objects that are close. This vision problem occurs when light rays entering the eye focused behind the retina rather than directly on it. The eyeball of a farsighted person is shorter than normal. A convex lens is used to correct this defect.

s: 'Joule' is related to energy in the same way as 'Pascal' is related to :
x: The joule is the unit of energy, just as the pascal is the unit of pressure.

s: Who discovered the rubber making process through the vulcanisation method ?
x: Charles Goodyear discovered vulcanisation of rubber (heating with sulphur) in 1839; John Dunlop is known for the pneumatic tyre.

s: Who among the following proposed that atom is indivisible?
x: John Dalton's atomic theory proposed that atoms are indivisible; this was later disproved by the discovery of subatomic particles.

s: Which one among the following is blind (extremely poor eyesight)?
Binary fission is a mode of
x: Binary fission, where a single cell divides into two, involves only one parent and no gametes, so it is asexual reproduction.

s: Mendel’s principles of inheritance are based on
x: Mendel's experiments were on garden pea plants, which reproduce sexually through gametes; his laws of segregation and independent assortment rely on gamete formation and fusion.

s: Density of water is
x: Water is densest at 4°C; below this it expands slightly as it approaches freezing, which is why ice floats.

s: What is the bond between two amino acids in a protein called ?
x: Amino acids in a protein are joined by peptide bonds (amide linkages formed between the carboxyl group of one and the amino group of the next); ester, glycosidic and phosphodiester bonds occur in lipids, carbohydrates and nucleic acids.

s: Which of the following is not unicellular ?
x: Euglena, Amoeba and Paramecium are single-celled organisms, whereas Hydra is a multicellular cnidarian, so it is the one that is not unicellular.

s: A man standing close to the platform at a railway station experiences a pulling force towards a fast moving train because of ………
o: gravitational force between train and man
pressure difference due to fast moving air in between
x: Fast-moving air near the train has lower pressure (Bernoulli's principle), so the higher pressure of the still air behind the man pushes him towards the train.

s: Which one among the following is not a chemical change?
x: Evaporation of water is a physical change of state with no new substance formed, whereas curdling of milk, ripening of fruit and burning of coal form new substances.

s: Which among the following is not a conductor of electricity?
x: Ebonite is hard rubber, an insulator; mercury, manganese and iron are metals and conduct electricity.

s: Which one among the following metals is more reactive than hydrogen?
x: Tin lies above hydrogen in the reactivity series, while mercury, copper and silver lie below it.

s: Which of the following waves can not be polarised?
x: Polarisation occurs only for transverse waves; radio, UV and infrared are electromagnetic (transverse), while ultrasonic sound waves are longitudinal and cannot be polarised.

s: Which of the following is the SI unit of temperature?
x: The kelvin is the SI unit of temperature; candela is luminous intensity, ampere is current, and the Reaumur scale is not an SI unit.

s: The movement of a horse drawn carriage is an example of which principle of physics.
x: A horse pushes the ground backward and the ground pushes it forward with an equal and opposite reaction, which is Newton's third law.

s: The impulse on a particle due to a force acting on it during a given time interval is equal to the change in its
x: By the impulse-momentum theorem, impulse (force x time) equals the change in momentum of the particle.

s: Which one of the following statement about the refractive index of a material medium with respect to air is correct?
o: It can be either positive or negative.
It is unity for all materials.
It is always greater than one.
x: Refractive index = speed of light in air/speed in medium, and light is slower in any material medium than in air, so it is always greater than one.

s: Bose-Einstein condensate is a
Nuclear sizes are expressed in a unit named
x: Nuclear sizes are of the order of 10^-15 m, which is called a fermi (femtometre); angstrom is 10^-10 m, and newton and tesla are units of force and magnetic field.

s: A conductor having some appreciable resistance is called a
x: A conductor that offers appreciable resistance to current is called a resistor, used to limit current in circuits.

s:
A liquid is kept in a glass beaker.
Which one of the following statement is correct regarding the pressure exerted by the liquid column at the base of the beaker ?
o: The pressure depends on the area of the base of the beaker.
The pressure depends on the height of liquid column.
The pressure does not depend on the height of liquid column.
The pressure neither depends on the area of the base of the beaker nor on the height of liquid column.
x: Liquid pressure at depth is P = h·rho·g, so it depends on the height of the liquid column (and density), not on the base area.

s: In respect of the difference of the gravitational force from electric and magnetic forces, which one of the following statements is true?
o: Gravitational forces is stronger than the other two.
Gravitational force is attractive only, whereas the electric and the magnetic forces are attractive as well as repulsive.
Gravitational force has a very short range.
Gravitational force is a long range force, while the other two are short range forces.
x: Gravity is always attractive, whereas electric and magnetic forces can attract or repel; gravity is actually the weakest, and all are long range.

s: Which one of the following statements about energy is correct?
o: Energy can be created as well as destroyed.
Energy can be created but not destroyed.
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed.
Energy cannot be created but can be destroyed.
x: By the law of conservation of energy, energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed from one form to another.

s: The energy of a photon, whose momentum is 10 Me V/c, where c is the speed of light, is given by
x: For a photon E = pc, so with p = 10 MeV/c the energy is 10 MeV.

s: The site of cellular respiration in animal cell is
The passage of an electric current through a conducting liquid causes … .
x: Passing current through a conducting liquid (electrolyte) causes electrolysis, which is a chemical reaction decomposing the substance at the electrodes.

s: Which of the following is not a mammal?
x: Fishes are cold-blooded gill-breathing vertebrates, whereas bats, whales and humans are mammals (warm-blooded, with mammary glands), so fishes is the odd one out.

s: Through the reaction of benzene and chlorine in the presence of catalyst say iron. Which of the following would be obtained?
x: In the presence of an iron (Lewis acid) catalyst, benzene undergoes electrophilic substitution with chlorine to give chlorobenzene. Benzene hexachloride forms only by addition under UV light.

s: Which one of the following contains powerful oxidative enzyme and helps in removing toxic substances from cells?
x: Peroxisomes contain oxidative enzymes such as catalase that detoxify harmful substances like hydrogen peroxide; lysosomes hold hydrolytic enzymes instead.

s: Which of the following is not a Primary function of a green leaf?
x: A leaf's primary functions are photosynthesis (food manufacture), gas exchange and transpiration. Conduction of food and water is done by the vascular tissue (xylem and phloem), not the leaf's primary function.

s:
Statement I Sound waves cannot propagate in vacuum. Statement II Sound waves are elastic waves and require a medium to propagate.
Codes
o: Both the statements are true and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
Both the statements are true, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
x: Sound is a mechanical (elastic) wave that needs a material medium, so it cannot travel through vacuum. Statement II is therefore the correct explanation of Statement I.

s:
Statement I The pitch of sound wave depends upon its frequency. Statement II The loudness of the sound wave depends upon its amplitude.
Codes
o: Both the statements are true and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
Both the statements are true, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
x: Pitch depends on frequency and loudness depends on amplitude. Both are true, but they are independent facts, so II does not explain I.

s:
Statement I All compounds contain more than one element. Statement II All compounds are heterogeneous mixtures.
Codes
o: Both the statements are individually true and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
Both the statements are individually true but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
x: A compound consists of two or more elements chemically combined, so Statement I is true. Compounds are homogeneous and are not mixtures, so Statement II is false.

s:
Statement I Glass is not considered as a true compound. Statement II Glass does not have a definite melting point.
Codes
o: Both the statements are individually true and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
Both the statements are individually true, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
x: Glass is an amorphous supercooled liquid, a mixture of silicates, with no sharp melting point. Because it lacks a definite melting point it is not a true compound, so II explains I.

s: Statement I Two ATP molecules are produced during anaerobic respiration. Statement II Glucose is converted into pyruvic acid through a series of reaction with a net gain of 2 ATP molecules.
o: Both the statements are individually true and the statement II is the correct explanation of the statement I.
Both the statements are individually true, but the statement II is not correct explanation of the statement I.
The statement I is true, but the statement II is false.
The statement I is false, but the statement II is true.
x: Glycolysis converts glucose to pyruvic acid with a net gain of 2 ATP, which is the only ATP produced in anaerobic respiration, so Statement II explains Statement I.

s:
Statement I Sound waves can travel through vacuum. Statement II Light is an electromagnetic wave and can travel through vacuum.
Codes
o: Both the statements are true and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
Both the statements are true, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
x: Sound needs a medium and cannot travel through vacuum, so Statement I is false. Light is an electromagnetic wave that can travel through vacuum, so Statement II is true.

s: Statement I While putting clothes for drying up, we spread them out. Statement II The rate of evaporation increases with an increase in surface area.
o: Both the statements are individually true and statement II is the correct expalanation of statement I.
Both the statements are individually true, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true
x: Evaporation happens at the surface, so a larger surface area speeds it up. This is why clothes are spread out to dry, so II explains I.

s: A thick paste of cement, sand and water is called
x: Mortar is a paste of cement, sand and water used as a binder in masonry. Concrete also contains coarse aggregate (gravel), and RCC is concrete reinforced with steel.

s: Which of the following is a major component of German silver?
x: German silver is an alloy of copper, zinc and nickel, so copper is its major component. It contains no silver.

s: The generic name of tusk shell or elephant tusk shell is
x: Dentalium is the genus of tusk shells (class Scaphopoda), named for their tusk-like shape. Chiton and Chaetoderma belong to other molluscan classes.

s: The correct relation between the radius of curvature R and focal length f of a spherical mirror is
x: For a spherical mirror the focal length is half the radius of curvature, so R = 2f.

s: What are the maximum numbers of electrons that can be present in a shell represented by shell number ‘n’?
x: By the Bohr-Bury rule, the maximum number of electrons in the nth shell is 2n².

s: This is not a use of a concave mirror
x: Concave mirrors are used in headlights, torches and shaving mirrors. Rear-view mirrors are convex, giving a wider field of view.

s: Which one of the following is the value of 1 nanometre?
x: 1 nm = 10⁻⁹ m = 10⁻⁷ cm, since 1 m = 100 cm.

s: Which of the following is monogamous?
x: Wolves form long-lasting monogamous pairs. Walrus, seals and deer are polygynous.

s: What is the yellow dust present in the middle of a flower called?
x: The yellow dust in the anthers of a flower is pollen, which carries the male gametes. Zygote, sperm and stomata do not fit.

s: At 20°C, the speed of sound in water approximately
x: The speed of sound in water is about 1500 m/s, much higher than in air (about 330 m/s), because sound travels faster in denser, less compressible media.

s: Crabs belongs to the Phylum
x: Crabs have jointed legs and an exoskeleton, so they belong to Phylum Arthropoda, not Mollusca.

s:
An acid is a substance which

I. is sour in taste.

II. turns red litmus paper into blue.
x: Acids taste sour. Turning red litmus blue is a property of bases, not acids (acids turn blue litmus red), so only I is correct.

s:
Consider the following statements.

I. Frogs can breathe by lungs as well as skin.

II. Gills are present in certain stages of life span of frogs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
x: Frogs breathe through lungs and moist skin as adults, and tadpoles have gills at an early stage, so both statements are correct.

s: If x the temperature of a system in Kelvin and y is the temperature of the system in °C, then the correct relation between them is
x: Kelvin temperature = Celsius temperature + 273, so x = 273 + y.

s: The absolute zero, i.e. temperature below which is not achievable, is about
x: Absolute zero is 0 K, which equals about -273°C. Option (2) is wrong because -273 K is not a valid temperature.

s: Which of the following is an aldehyde?
x: Propanal (CH3CH2CHO) has the -CHO aldehyde group. Propanol is an alcohol, propanone a ketone and propyne an alkyne.

s: A Parenchyma cell which stores ergastic substance is known as
x: An idioblast is a specialised parenchyma cell that stores ergastic substances such as crystals or oils.

s: Snails belong to Phylum
x: Snails are soft-bodied animals with a shell, so they belong to Phylum Mollusca.

s: The frequency (in Hz) of a note that is one octave higher than 500 Hz is
x: One octave higher means double the frequency, so 500 Hz becomes 1000 Hz.

s: If a body is whirled in a circle the work done on it …………
x: In circular motion the force (centripetal) is perpendicular to the displacement, so the work done is zero.

s: The oxidation number of nickel in K4[Ni(CN)4] is
x: CN is a -1 ligand, so four CN give -4 and K4 gives +4. The sum of these is zero, so Ni must be 0, which is the usual case for Ni(0) carbonyl-type complexes.

s: How many watts are there in metric horse power?
x: The notes give 1 horsepower as 746 W (the British value), but the metric horsepower is 735.5 W, about 736 W, so option (1) is correct.

s: A current I flows through a resistor. A source maintains a potential difference of V across the resistor. The energy supplied by the source in time t is
x: Energy supplied = power x time = VI x t = VIt.

s: What is thick vein present in the middle of the leaf called?
x: The thick central vein of a leaf is called the midrib.

s: Insulators have resistivity of the order of
x: Insulators have very high resistivity, of the order of 10^12 to 10^17 ohm-metre.

s: Pollens are produced in
x: Pollen grains are produced in the anther of the stamen.

s: In which part of the female flower, fertilisation take place?
x: Fertilisation takes place in the ovary, where the ovules are present. The pollen tube grows through the style to reach it.

s: Which among the following is a male part of a flower ?
x: The stamen (anther plus filament) is the male part of a flower. Stigma, style and pistil are female parts.

s: Which one of the following oxides dissolves in water?
x: Na2O is a basic oxide of an alkali metal that dissolves in water to form NaOH. CuO, Al2O3 and Fe2O3 are insoluble.

s: If formula of sodium salt of an anion X is Na 2X , then the formula of its aluminium salt would be
x: Na2X means X carries a 2- charge. Al is 3+, so the formula is criss-crossed to Al2X3.

s: In the context of genetic disorder, consider the following. A women suffer from colour blindness, while her husband does not suffer from it. They have a son and a daughter. In this context, which one of the following statement is most probably correct?
o: Both children suffer from colour blindness.
Daughter suffer from colour blindness while son does not suffer from it.
Both children do not suffer from colour blindness.
Son suffers from colour blindness, while daughter does not suffer from it.
x: Colour blindness is X-linked recessive. A colour-blind mother (XcXc) passes Xc to all children. The son gets Xc from her and Y from the father, so he is affected. The daughter gets a normal X from the father, so she is a carrier but not affected.

s: Who among the following first discovered cell?
x: Robert Hooke first observed and named cells in 1665 in cork slices under a microscope. Leeuwenhoek saw living cells later.

s: According to which one of the following laws it is indicated that when two or more gases react with one another, their volumes bear a simple ratio?
x: Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes says gases react in volumes that bear a simple whole-number ratio.

s: Which of the following is warm blooded animal ?
x: Bat is a mammal and so is warm-blooded. Shark, snake and lizard are cold-blooded.

s: In terms of the evolution of organisms, which one among the following is the most avanced?
x: Mammals are the most advanced class of these. Bat is a mammal, while Aves and Pisces rank lower.

s: Damage to the apical meristem of a growing young plant will affect the
x: The apical meristem is responsible for growth in length. Damage to it stops the plant from growing taller.

s:
Match the following
List I
List II

A. Birds
1. Palaeobiology

B. Inheritance
2. Ecology

C. Environment
3. Ornithology

D. Fossil
4. Genetics
Codes A B C D A B C D
x: Birds are studied in ornithology, inheritance in genetics, environment in ecology and fossils in palaeobiology. This gives 3 4 2 1.

s: ........ states that the total current entering a junction is equal to the total current leaving the junction.
x: Kirchhoff's first (current) law states that the current entering a junction equals the current leaving it, which follows from conservation of charge.

s: .......... .is not related to gases.
x: Boyle's, Charles's and Avogadro's laws are gas laws. Joule's law concerns the heating effect of current.

s: How much calories are there in a Joule?
x: 1 calorie = 4.18 J, so 1 J = about 0.24 calorie.

s: The motion of a freely falling body is an example of ........... accelerated motion.
x: A freely falling body has a constant acceleration g, so its motion is uniformly accelerated.

s: Why does a cannon recoil after firing?
A body is acted upon by two unequal forces in opposite directions, but not in one line. The effect is that the body will have
o: neither the rotational nor the translational motion.
rotational as well as translational motion.

s: Which of the following is a heterogeneous mixture?
x: A suspension has visible particles that are not uniformly distributed, so it is heterogeneous. A solution is homogeneous.

s: Boiling point of water is .... .
x: Water boils at 100°C, which is 212°F.

s: The absolute zero temperature is 0°K. In °C unit, which one of the following is the absolute zero temperature?
x: 0 K equals -273.15°C.

s: Which finger shows the direction of current in Fleming’s left hand rule?
x: In Fleming's left-hand rule the thumb shows force, the forefinger shows the field and the middle finger shows the current direction.

s: Silver ware turns black after a period of time due to the formation of
x: Silver reacts with hydrogen sulphide in the air to form black silver sulphide.

s: Which one of the following represents the correct order of electron releasing tendency of metals?
x: In the reactivity series Zn is more reactive than Cu, which is more reactive than Ag. So the electron-releasing tendency is Zn > Cu > Ag.

s: The wing of a bat and the wing of a bird are the examples of .............. limbs.
x: Bat and bird wings have the same function but different structure and origin, so they are analogous organs.

s: The heat produced by current in wire during time t is determined by ……… .
x: Joule's law of heating gives H = I²Rt: heat grows with the square of current, with resistance and with time. Options 1 and 3 omit a factor, and option 2 uses I instead of I².

s: Any one parameter is not good enough to demonstrate growth through the life of a flowering plant because
o: lateral meristems appear later in life.
apical meristems contribute to elongation while lateral meristems increase girth.
increase in protoplasm is difficult to measure directly.

s: As the object covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time, it is said to be in ......... motion.
x: Covering unequal distances in equal time intervals means the velocity is changing, which is non-uniform motion. Uniform motion covers equal distances in equal intervals.

s: Which one of the following tissues is responsible for increase of girth in the stem of a plant?
x: Lateral meristem (vascular cambium and cork cambium) divides sideways and so increases the girth of the stem. Intercalary meristem only increases length.

s: Which among the following has segmented body ?
The sensation of sound persists in the human brain for about
x: Persistence of hearing is about 0.1 s, so an echo needs a gap of at least 0.1 s to be heard as distinct from the original sound.

s: More density of the particles in the medium through which sound travels, creates more ……… and vice versa.
x: In a sound wave, greater density of particles in the medium corresponds to greater pressure (compressions are high-density, high-pressure regions), and vice versa.

s: ………being a higher category, is the assemblage of families which exhibit a few similar characters.
x: In the taxonomic hierarchy, an order is an assemblage of related families. Species and genus are lower categories, and class is a higher category that groups orders.

s: If an object is at rest, then the time (X-axis) versus distance (Y-axis) graph
x: For a body at rest the distance stays constant as time passes, so the distance-time graph is a horizontal line with zero slope.

s: The angle in which a cricket ball should be hit to travel maximum horizontal distance is
x: The projectile range R = u²sin2θ/g is maximum when sin2θ = 1, i.e. θ = 45°.

s: Magnetic meridian is an imaginary
x: The magnetic meridian is the vertical plane passing through the magnetic axis, that is, through the magnetic north and south poles of the Earth. It is not just a line.

s: Which of the following is the correct sequence of levels of hierarchy of classification of organisms from higher to lower ?
x: The hierarchy runs Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species, so Phylum-Class-Order-Family-Genus is the correct descending order.

s: The term ‘Meiosis’ was coined by
x: The term meiosis was coined by Farmer and Moore in 1905. Fleming described mitosis.

s: Which of the following pair represent the Correct pair of reproductive parts of a flower ?
x: The stamens (male) and carpels (female) are the reproductive parts of a flower. Sepals and petals are accessory, non-reproductive whorls.

s:
Statement I Complex tissue is made up of more then one type of cells. Statement II Meristems are examples of permanent tissue.
Codes
o: Statement I is correct, but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.
Both Statements I and II are correct.
Both Statements I and II are incorrect.
x: Complex tissues such as xylem and phloem contain more than one cell type, so Statement I is correct. Meristems are dividing tissues, not permanent tissues, so Statement II is wrong.

s:
Statement I A compass needle placed near a current-carrying wire will get deflected. Statement II A current-carrying wire creates magnetic field around it.
Codes
o: Statement I and statement II are correct and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I
Statement I and statement II are correct, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I
Statement I is correct, but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, but statement II is correct
x: A current-carrying wire produces a magnetic field around it (Oersted), and this field deflects a nearby compass needle. So II correctly explains I.

s: Arrangement of leaves in a plant is called as ……… .
x: The arrangement of leaves on a stem is called phyllotaxy. The other terms are not botanical terms for this.

s: Two identical solid pieces, one of gold and other of silver, when immersed completely in water exhibit equal weights. When weighed in air (given that, density of gold is greater than that of silver),
o: the gold piece will weigh more.
the silver piece will weigh more.
Both silver and gold pieces weigh equal.
weighing will depend on their masses.
x: Equal weights in water means W - buoyant force is equal for the two pieces. Both pieces have the same volume, so the buoyant force is equal, and the weights in air would be equal. The question seems to describe pieces of different volume, though: the denser gold piece has smaller volume, experiences less buoyancy, so it needs a smaller air weight than silver for equal water weights. Hence silver weighs more in air.

s: How many elements are there in the 5th Period of Modern Periodic Table?
x: The 5th period begins with Rb and ends with Xe and includes the 4d transition series, giving 18 elements.

s: A person is standing on a frictionless horizontal ground. How can he move by a certain distance on this ground?
x: With no friction, he cannot push against the ground. Sneezing expels air and, by conservation of momentum, pushes him in the opposite direction. Jumping, running and rolling all need friction.

s: JJ Thomson’s proposed model of atom is generally called ………… model.
x: Thomson's atomic model is called the plum pudding model, with electrons embedded in a positively charged sphere like plums in a pudding.

s: When the direction of motion of coil is perpendicular to the electromagnetic field, then the value of induced current is ……… .

A spring can be used to determine the mass m of an object in two ways : I by measuring the extension in the spring due to the object and II by measuring the oscillation period for the given mass.
Which of these methods can be used in a space-station orbiting the earth?
x: In orbit there is effective weightlessness, so a hanging mass does not stretch the spring. The oscillation period T = 2π√(m/k) depends on mass and not on gravity, so only the oscillation method works.

s: When temperature difference between liquid and its surroundings is doubled, the rate of loss of heat will
x: By Newton's law of cooling, for a small temperature difference the rate of heat loss is proportional to that difference. Doubling the difference doubles the rate.

s: Which statement is incorrect for animals belonging to class of Chondrichthyes ?
o: Notochord is persistent only at larval stage, after that it disappears.
x: Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fishes) have a notochord that persists throughout life, so the statement that it disappears after the larval stage is incorrect.

s: The atomic weights are expressed in terms of atomic mass unit. Which one of the following is used as standard?
x: The atomic mass unit is defined as 1/12 of the mass of a carbon-12 atom, so carbon-12 is the standard.

s: If we plot a graph between volume V and inverse of pressure p (i.e. 1/p) for an ideal gas at constant temperature T, the curve so obtained is a
x: By Boyle's law, pV = constant at fixed T, so V = constant × (1/p). This is a straight line through the origin in a V vs 1/p graph; a hyperbola would result from V vs p.

s: Which one of the following force is non-central and non-conservative?
x: Friction depends on velocity direction and the path, and it dissipates energy, so it is non-central and non-conservative. Electric and gravitational forces are central and conservative.

s: Which of the following is the maximum number of electrons that can be present in M-shell?
x: The maximum number of electrons in a shell is 2n². For the M shell (n=3) this is 18.

s: The number of maximum electrons in N shell is
x: The maximum number of electrons in a shell is 2n². For the N shell (n=4) this is 32.

s: If a physical quantity has the units- ampere meters per second squared, then what are it’s dimensions?
x: Ampere is the unit of current, with dimension I (or A), and metre per second squared gives L T^-2. The combined dimensions are [I L T^-2].

s: Magnification is
o: observed size of specimen actual size.
x: Magnification is the ratio of the observed (image) size to the actual size of the specimen.

s: On what basis Greek thinker Aristotle classified the animals for the first time ?
x: Aristotle first classified animals on the basis of their habitat (land, water, air).

s: A rectangular coil of copper wire is rotating in a magnetic field. The direction of the induced current changes once in each?
x: In an AC generator the induced current reverses direction every half rotation, so the direction changes once per half revolution.

s: Which one of the following features is an indication for modification of stem of a plant?
x: The potato is a stem tuber and its 'eyes' are nodes with buds, which indicate a modified stem. Onion scales are modified leaves, pea tendrils are modified leaves or leaflets, and carrot is a root.

s: Fruit of which of the following plant is found in the underground soil?
x: The peanut flower's stalk bends down after fertilisation and pushes the fruit (pod) into the soil. Potato, carrot and onion are underground stems or roots, not fruits.
